newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules suit vs Bessemer Trust should proceed.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules suit vs Bessemer Trust should proceed.

text.p: A federal judge has ruled that a lawsuit against investment advisor Bessemer Trust brought by an investor who allegedly lost millions of dollars should proceed, the plaintiff's lawyers said Thursday.

The ruling, by Judge John Keenan of the U.S. district court in Manhattan, allows trial by jury of claims of fraud and gross negligence against Bessemer by investor David Levy, said the law firm of Brock, Fensterstock, Silverstein, McAuliffe & Wade LLC.
The ruling was handed down on July 30, after Bessemer had filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit, the law firm said, adding that Keenan held that all but one of Levy's claims were sufficiently plead.

Levy, who is chief executive of Franklin Health Inc, a New Jersey-based health care management company, had entrusted about $8 million of Corning Inc stock to Bessemer, said Blair Festerstock, Levy's attorney.
Levy had asked Bessemer to provide his funds with downward price protection against losses, Fensterstock said.
"They failed to do that; they said it was impossible to do," he said.
After seeking advice from a competing firm, Levy found that the protection he was seeking could be had in the form of European-style options, Fensterstock said.
But because Bessemer failed to advise Levy about such a protection, he suffered more than $4 million in losses, Fensterstock said.
Fensterstock said that, with the ruling, the case should be ready for trial in mid-December.
Richard Davis, legal counsel for Bessemer, said the investment advisor's position was that Levy's claims were not legally sufficient and that his complaint was "completely without merit."
"We are confident that at the trial we will be completely vindicated," Davis said.
